title: Tokyo Night Festival Lantern Placement
description: Students explore a miniature Tokyo street scene and learn about traditional Japanese lantern festivals by placing lanterns at designated cultural landmarks. Each placement triggers an educational popup explaining the significance of lanterns in Japanese culture, and students must correctly answer quiz questions to illuminate each lantern and progress through the lesson.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements an interactive educational lantern festival experience. Load LittlestTokyo.glb as the central scene scaled to fit a 20-unit bounding box centered at origin. Load Lantern.glb and create 5 cloned instances, initially arranged in a row along the bottom of the screen as a draggable inventory bar rendered with CSS overlay. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (15, 12, 15) looking at the origin with OrbitControls limited to a 60-degree polar angle range so students can orbit but not flip below the scene. Add ambient light at intensity 0.3 and a dim directional light at intensity 0.4 to simulate nighttime. Mark 5 glowing circular drop zones on the Tokyo scene using semi-transparent green ring sprites at varied positions across the model (rooftops, street corners, bridge). Implement drag-and-drop: when a user clicks a lantern in the inventory, it attaches to the mouse via raycasting. When dropped near a valid drop zone (within 1.5 units), snap the lantern to that position and display an HTML overlay panel with a short educational fact about Japanese lantern traditions (prepare 5 unique facts). Each panel includes a multiple-choice quiz question with 3 options. If the student selects the correct answer, animate the lantern glowing bright orange using a PointLight child with intensity ramping from 0 to 2 over 1 second, and play a success chime. If incorrect, shake the lantern with a quick oscillation animation and let them retry. Track progress in a top-right HUD showing lanterns placed (e.g., 3/5) and score. When all 5 lanterns are correctly placed and lit, trigger a celebration: smoothly animate the camera in a 360-degree orbit around the scene over 8 seconds while all lantern lights pulse gently using sine-wave intensity modulation. Use GLTFLoader from CDN, enable tone mapping and shadow maps for atmosphere. Ensure all animations use the built-in AnimationMixer for LittlestTokyo so its ambient animations play continuously.
